body:
Second read (read-only, not built) of head 59b42c7276258c7722476d93add71d09abcd933f.

**Verdict: one defect found by reading (medium), and two documentation gaps.** No gouge path found. Auto is byte-identical.

## Defect 1 (medium): Outside still cuts full slots when the rings split

File: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs:51-58` (`PassStart::rank`), used at `crates/motion/src/machining2d/waterscan.rs:136-143`.

The rank puts every counter-clockwise loop before every clockwise loop. When a band has a narrow part, the ring at offset k* splits into pieces. Each piece is a new region, so its loop is counter-clockwise (`outer.push(l.is_ccw())`, `waterscan.rs:109`). A piece boundary has a stock-side arc and a part-side arc. Outside cuts these pieces (k* + 1 to the core) before the hole rings (k* down to 0).

Scenario (hand trace): stock reach 100 x 40, a round part of radius 15 at the center, tool R4, step 4. The gap at the top and the bottom is 5 mm, so the ring splits at k = 1 into a left piece and a right piece. Order for Outside:

1. CCW k = 0, the stock-edge ring (the tool is outside the stock: correct).
2. CCW k = 1, left piece. On its part-side arc (radius 19) the tool covers radius 15 to 23. No ring cut this material before. Result: a full-width slot along the arc.
3. CCW k = 1, right piece: the same full slot.
4. The piece rings to the core, then CW k = 0, the part wall ring (last: correct).

The fig8 pin has the same shape: a box 5 mm past the part gives a 5 mm gap at the lobe tips, so the ring splits at k = 1. The corner and waist pieces then have part-side arcs that cut a full slot. The pin checks only the first and the last move of each level, so it does not see this.

The claim "no ring is a full slot" is in the rank doc comment, in `docs/decisions/3316-pass-start-shared.md`, in the hint text (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pass_start_row.rs:16`) and in the MCP skill row. That claim is not true after a split. This is not a gouge: the cut stays in the certified area. It is the tool-load defect of #3316, made smaller but not removed. Recommendation: rank a post-split piece by the distance of each arc to the cut side, or cut the hole rings of offset k before the pieces of offset k + 1. At a minimum, remove the claim and add a note on the toolpath.

## Documentation gaps

- Outside on a closed pocket: the first ring is the pocket wall ring at k = 0, a full slot on the finish wall. The PR body says this. The user guide (`site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md:291-299`) and the hint do not say it. The user gets no warning.
- Inside on an Outside band, and Inside on a pocket with an island: the first ring is the part or island wall ring, a full slot on the finish wall. The guide and the hint do not say it. No warning.

## Points checked

1. Auto: `rank` gives `kmax - k`. A stable ascending sort on it gives the same order as the old stable `sort_by_key(Reverse(k))`. `outer` is pushed with `loops` under the same condition (`waterscan.rs:107-110`), so the zip is aligned. `plan_passes` (`pocket_plan.rs:23`) calls Auto. The callers `pocket_hsm.rs:74` and `machining3d/hsm.rs:146,150,260` stay on Auto. `pocket_entered_with_relief` and `pocket_avoid_with_relief` call the new functions with Auto. No golden file is in the diff.
2. Hand trace of an annulus with no split: CCW k = 0 .. kmax, then CW kmax .. 0. The first ring is at the stock edge, each next ring steps one stepover, and the last ring is the part wall ring of the center region (stock to leave is in the center offset). Correct for this case. Inside on a closed pocket with no island is the same as Auto.
3. Entries and links: the first ring of the new order gets the entry from `descend` (`ladder_links.rs:58`) inside the certified area. A pass restart goes through `pass_link` (`ladder_links.rs:154`). `plunge_law::into_solid` (`plunge_law.rs:73`) reads the moves already posted (`column_cleared`), so it follows the new order. Each start on uncut stock gets the helix or ramp. A keep-down link (`link_proof`, `ladder_links.rs:220`) must stay in the certified area and cross no planned ring, so it stays in one band. It is a feed, not a rapid. A level keep-down link runs at `prev_z`, which is fully cut. No rapid below the retract plane crosses uncut stock by reading.
4. Rest (`rest2d.rs:289`) is forced to Auto. HSM and the 3-D pocket stay on Auto. "Do not touch" (`pocket_avoid.rs:145`) takes the new order, and no test runs it with Outside. Corner relief spurs are added after the order (`pocket_emit.rs:127`); I find no order dependency there. Offset2D uses `PocketStrategy::Waterline` only, so no Zigzag or Adaptive path ignores the choice.
5. Command law: the field is a plain `OpParams` field, so `EditOperationParams` writes it and undo restores it (pinned). serde refuses an unknown word (pinned). `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]` loads an old file as Auto. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. All new files are under 400 lines (largest: `mcp/edit.rs` 389, `pocket.rs` 383). The new `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` is at `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:293` on `pocket_over_with_relief` (8 arguments). It has a reason, and the decision file says why the field is not in `PocketParams`. I find that acceptable for this PR.
6. Pins: `fig8_outside_offset_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` proves the start and the end of each level only. `fig8_auto_offset_keeps_every_lateral_rapid_at_the_clearance_plane` proves that the Auto first ring is not at the stock edge; it does not prove a byte-identical Auto (the goldens do that in part). The pins do not prove the engagement along the level, so Defect 1 passes them.
7. PR body: `Process change: yes` is correct (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`), and `PROCESS_VERSION` is not changed. The `Changelog:` line is there, but it says "no longer slots the stock", which Defect 1 contradicts. The decision file is there. The 242 reached heavy steps are "not run". By AGENTS.md (#2568) the PR is not ready until they run on the final head.

## Not judged without a run

- The real ring topology of the fig8 pin and the size of the slot on the part-side arcs.
- The helix site that `plan` picks at the stock-edge ring and at the pocket wall ring.
- The engagement of the chain chords between rings.
- Outside with "Do not touch" picks.
- The heavy lanes and the UI.

The review finding is confirmed. The fix needs a new ring geometry (open level curves clipped to the cutter-center area), not a new order of closed rings. That work is `effort:max`. Issue #3316 is escalated to `effort:max`; the analysis is in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3316#issuecomment-7077876119. This PR stays a draft with head 59b42c727 and no new push.

ready for a re-read: head 9939a6238ff087f735b93ec2a093e2bd9e35d3d6. The ring law of Inside and Outside is new (level curves of the start side, open pieces, lead-ins from cut floor, "Pass start" warnings). The PR body has the red-then-green readings, the per-binary quick results and 55 heavy steps (0 failed); 188 reached heavy steps are listed as not run. The PR stays a draft.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head 9939a6238ff087f735b93ec2a093e2bd9e35d3d6.

**Verdict: one defect found by reading. It is a blocker (a silent leftover).** I found no gouge and no rapid through stock by reading. Auto is the old planner.

## Defect 1 (blocker): Outside leaves the inside of a nested material area uncut, with no warning

File: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs:79`.

```rust
let filled = Region::new(region.loops().iter().filter(|l| l.is_ccw()).cloned().collect())?;
```

`Region::new` reads loops by nesting parity (`geo2d.rs`, `normalize`, step 2). A CCW loop that is nested in another CCW loop becomes a hole. Thus "filled" is not "the outer edge with the holes filled" when the region has material inside a hole (depth 2).

Scenario: a region with an outer loop A, a hole B in it, and a material loop C inside B. Examples: a pocket with a hollow boss (a tube) whose bore floor is at the pocket floor, or a sketch with three nested profiles. Hand trace for Outside, with tool radius r:

1. `filled` = A minus C, because C is nested and becomes a hole.
2. `fc = filled.offset(-off)` has a hole: C grown by `off`.
3. Every ring j (`fc.offset(-j * step)`, line 89) has C grown by `off + j * step` as a hole. No ring piece lands in the centre component of C.
4. In `sides` (line 131), the boundary of the centre component of C is outside `fc`, so it becomes ring 0. It gets no wall piece.
5. Result: component C gets only one closed ring along its own boundary. All material of C farther than 2r from its edge stays uncut at full depth.

The PR has a fixture with this shape: `ringed` in `the_wall_first_and_narrow_cases_are_named_on_the_path` (`crates/motion/tests/pass_start_levels.rs:208-212`). The disc of radius 15 in the ring part is material C. Its centre area is a disc of radius 11. The tool sweeps radius 7 to 15 only, so a disc of radius 7 (about 154 mm2) stays standing. The test asserts the narrow warning only. By my trace that warning comes from the band (circle 31 at 45 degrees, far from ring 2), not from C. The test does not measure the leftover. The only note for C is the wall-first note ("each level starts with a cut of the full tool width along that wall"), which does not say that material stays. A later operation that expects a cleared floor hits this post at full depth.

The Outside containment band of the app removes the holes of the part (`crates/app/src/operation/boundary.rs:119-121`, `connected_to`), so fig8 does not show this. A closed pocket region with a nested island bore does show it.

Recommended fix: build `filled` with `Region::union_all` of the CCW loops, as `reach_past_edge` does (`crates/app/src/operation/boundary.rs:119`). Then C is inside `filled`, the rings of the outer edge pass through C and are clipped to its centre area, and the boundary of C becomes a wall. Add a shape-mask check (`assert_bounded_leftover`) for `ringed` with Outside and Inside, and for a pocket with a hollow boss. Inside does not have this defect by my trace: `holes = filled - region` gives B minus C, and the rings grow into C from its edge.

## Minor

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs` grows from 394 to 401 lines (the 400-line law). `levels.rs` was over the limit before (443 -> 454).
- Completeness has no general check in the planner. The argument is by reading (below) and by the three fixtures. A cheap check after the plan (the swept discs of the passes against the region) would make a leftover visible. It is not necessary for this PR if Defect 1 is fixed.

## Points checked

1. **Gouge.** Ring j pieces are `center.clip_ring` results (`level_rings.rs:184`). Each sub-segment between two crossings has its midpoint inside `center`, so each kept piece lies in the cutter-centre area. Ring 0 and the walls are pieces of the boundary of `center` itself. `off = r + stock_to_leave` (line 51), so each wall piece keeps the stock to leave. Join chords and lead-in chords both go through `linkable` (`level_order.rs:225-233`). Its first test is `chord_clears(center, e, s)` (`chord_clear.rs:40`): the two ends must be in or on `center`, and the complete chord is split at each vertex touch and tested piece by piece. That is the wall check for the full swept chord, also at a concave corner, a neck or a boundary point. The 0.9-radius test is only the engagement law. In `pocket_avoid` the `center` is `level_center`, so the "Do not touch" keep-outs are walls. Wall direction: `sides` walks the wall pieces in the reverse of ring 0 (`back`, line 137), so the material is on the right for climb and on the left for conventional. A hole wall that is not split is one closed wall pass. A wall that ring 0 splits is several open pieces, joined by chords where `linkable` permits.
2. **`clip_line.rs`.** Each segment is split at all proper, touching and collinear crossings (lines 165-200). Each sub-piece is kept by the parity of its midpoint. A vertex on the boundary is safe, because each segment is split on its own. A tangent touch splits the segment, but the two halves have the same parity, so the stretch continues. The wrap of a ring is joined (lines 69-75). Repeated points are removed in `checked`, and zero-length stretches in `retain` (line 122). NaN gives `Invalid` and a large value gives `OutOfRange`. No loop runs without a bound, and no index is unchecked. A stretch exactly on the boundary is decided by the half-open ray rule. `sides` avoids that case with the `SIDE_EPS` shrink and grow. For `curves`, the case can occur only where a level curve is collinear with a wall, and the wall pass cuts it. The 3 unit tests cover: a crossing, a hole crossing, a whole ring, a ring fully outside, the wrap, an empty path, one point, zero length, NaN, out-of-range, an empty region, and a path along the boundary (the last only gives an answer; its result is not asserted). Not covered: a vertex exactly on the boundary, a tangent touch, a collinear overlap in the middle of a segment.
3. **Rapids and links.** The join chords and lead-ins are part of a pass (cutting feeds). Between passes, `pass_link` (`ladder_links.rs:154-215`) gives a feed only for a proved keep-down link. Each other link is a rapid at `clearance_z` or `hop_z`. `through_cut` (lines 221-228) samples the chord at a quarter radius and calls `plunge_law::column_cleared(b.moves(), q, z, r)`. That reads the moves posted up to that moment (so it follows the order) and accepts only a cutting move at or below the current `z`. Earlier levels are higher, so they cannot prove it. Note: `column_cleared` proves the centre core (0.5 r), not the full disc. That is acceptable for a feed. The 93 lateral rapids on fig8 Outside go by these rules. The heavy test `fig8_outside_offset_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` asserts no lateral rapid below clearance and no `RapidInStock` warning. I did not run it. With "Hop below clearance" on, the height of `hop_z` is the law of #3318 and #3319 (still open), and this PR does not change it.
4. **Entries.** A lead-in starts at a vertex of a cut already walked at this level (`lead_in`, lines 239-248), so `into_solid` is false there and the plunge goes into a cleared column. A piece with no lead-in that starts in stock goes through `pass_link` with `into_solid` true: `entry_restart` or `restart` (helix or ramp), or the `plunge_law::guard` refusal for a non-centre-cutting tool. Ring 0 has no lead-in and gets the entry from `descend`. #3397: the two helices are each certified in the entry area, and the pass coverage does not depend on them. By reading, it is a verifier report and a lost cleared column, not a gouge or an uncut post.
5. **Completeness.** By reading, for a correct `filled`: each centre point lies between two level curves of the outer edge. Where a hole hides the start side, the hole wall is nearer than the hidden curve. The core of the last ring is at most one step from it, and `validate` keeps the step at or below one radius for rings (`pocket.rs`). A band narrower than the tool gives the refusal "pocket is narrower than the tool". A band narrower than the tool plus one step gives the narrow note. Several holes: each is a wall. Several separate outer loops: each is a component. An open boundary is closed by the area law before the planner. Nested material: Defect 1.
6. **Auto.** `git diff origin/main 9939a6238 -- crates/motion/src/machining2d/waterscan.rs` is empty. `ring_plan` returns `plan_passes` for Auto (line 57). `cleared_links` is false for Auto, and the pre-drilled re-seat does not change for Auto. `rest2d.rs` passes `StartSide::default()`. The HSM branch and the 3-D pocket call `plan_passes` directly. No golden file is in the diff. The command, the project key, the MCP tool and the Passes-tab row did not change after head 59b42c727 (`git diff --stat 59b42c727 9939a6238`).
7. **Tests.** The meter (`shape_mask.rs:143-205`) measures the contact width at each grid step of each planar feed against the swept state at that moment, and only then sweeps the step. It is sound for planar feeds. It does not measure helices, ramps or plunges. Each of the three motion fixtures runs `assert_no_overcut` against the disc area. The pin fixture also runs `avoid_hits`, but it has no leftover assert. The two fig8 Outside tests are `#[ignore = "heavy lane (#3316 fig8 Outside): ..."]`, which obeys the Testing rules. They have no light twin, but the five default tests in `pass_start_levels.rs` pin Outside in the quick tier.
8. **Law.** I found no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or `unreachable!` in non-test code. All indexes are bounded (`groups[c]` is clamped, `windows`, `% len`). The clip is in `geometry`, the planner is in `motion`, and `pass_start_stock.rs` uses `OpParams`, `SrcRef` and `Material` of the operation (document glue). There is no new dependency between our crates. The warning texts are plain English. The body has `Process change: yes` and does not change `PROCESS_VERSION`. 55 of 243 reached heavy steps ran (0 failed). 188 are "not run", and "not run" is not a pass (#2568).

## Not judged without a run

- The leftover of Defect 1 on `ringed` (I expect about 154 mm2 by hand).
- The fig8 Outside rapids, the heights of the 93 hops, and the full-width count.
- Arc fit and corner fillets on the new open pieces and join chords.
- Runtime on large areas: the clip is O(segments x edges) with a box test only (fig8 Outside 26.6 s against 9.5 s in debug).
- The 188 heavy steps that did not run.

One open PR still uses this branch as its GitHub base, #3422 (Trochoidal Slot). Please retarget #3422 to `main` before merging this PR or deleting its branch. This keeps its review thread and test results open.

Circular #3441 and Slot #3401 now target `main`. Their reviewed commits remain `c9b1ed4a6` and `3572ca334`. Slot will wait for both this PR and #3387 to merge before taking a fresh merge of `main` and running its gate.

ready for a re-read: head a91eb11d307a890e24b89a8e658c7ba842e0c219. Fix of the third read: each nested material part is planned from its own edges, and a completeness guard falls back to Auto with a named warning. Red on 9939a6238: the ring-part fixture left 153.7 mm2 at Outside, and the hollow-boss pocket had 1126 disallowed interior cells. Both are green now. All 37 touched binaries are green, and clippy is clean. The whole reached heavy plan ran: 243 steps, 0 failed. The PR stays a draft.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head a91eb11d307a890e24b89a8e658c7ba842e0c219.

**Verdict: no defect found by reading.** The blocker of my read of 9939a6238 (comment 7079896741, the nested-material leftover) is closed by reading. I found no gouge, no rapid through stock and no silent leftover. Two notes follow (no blockers).

## 1. The blocker is closed

`material_parts` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs:160-187`) makes one part for each counter-clockwise loop, with the holes directly inside it. A hole goes to a part only if no other counter-clockwise loop inside that part also contains the hole (`nearer`, lines 172-179). The loop runs over all counter-clockwise loops at all depths, so the rule is the same at each depth. Hand trace for A (pocket) > B (boss, hole) > C (bore, material) > D (hole) > E (material):

- Part A gets hole B. D is in C, and C is in A, so D is not A's hole.
- Part C gets hole D. Part E has no hole.

For each part, `filled` is only the part's own outer loop (line 112), so it has no hole. Then `c = center ∩ part` (line 108).

Outside in C (`ringed`: bore radius 15, tool radius 4, step 4): `fc` is the disc of radius 11. Ring 0 is circle 11 (all of C's boundary, `sides`). Ring 1 is circle 7 and ring 2 is circle 3, both from `fc.offset(-j * step)`. `fc.offset(-12)` is empty, so the loop stops. The disc on circle 3 sweeps radius 0 to 7, so the core is cut. The hollow-boss bore (radius 10) gives circles 6 and 2. Ring 0 of a bore is a wall in the stock, and the wall-first note names it. Inside in A uses only A's holes (`holes = filled - part`, line 113), and the clip to `c` keeps its rings out of C.

Note (not a defect): `material_parts` tests one first point of each loop. Where a hole touches its outer loop at that point, the half-open rule can drop the hole from the part. `c` comes from `center`, so the cut area does not change. Only the Inside start side of that part can change, so this is not a safety case.

## 2. The guard

`unswept` (lines 75-78) sweeps a disc of radius `r * (1 - 1e-3)` along each pass (`Region::sweep`, round joins, with flats that lie inside the true disc). It subtracts that area from `center` (the cutter-centre area), erodes the result by 0.05 mm, and measures the area. The comparison is conservative:

- The disc is a little smaller than the tool.
- Helices, ramps and keep-down links are not counted, but they only cut more.
- An unswept centre point is a material point that no disc reached: a standing post.

The guard does not read the band between `center` and the region wall. By construction, ring 0 and the walls together walk the full boundary of `center`, so that band is cut. The guard checks the interior, and the interior is where the old defect was.

Threshold: after the 0.05 mm erosion, a leftover passes only if it is narrower than about 0.1 mm, or if it is a post less than about 0.46 mm in diameter (π(ρ - 0.05)² ≤ 0.1 gives ρ ≤ 0.23 mm). The rings are at most one step apart, and `validate` keeps the step at or below one radius. A structural miss of this plan is therefore a large area, as the 153.7 mm² case was, and not a pin. I find the threshold acceptable. Auto itself has no such guard.

Fallback scope: `ring_plan` changes the whole plan of the area it gets.

- In `pocket_over_with_relief`, the plan is made one time for all levels. The fallback is then for the whole operation, and the levels do not mix.
- In `pocket_avoid`, the plan is made for each level on `level_center`. One level can then be Auto while another level uses the start-side plan. One level never mixes two orders.

The ladder already walks a different plan on each level in `pocket_avoid`. The level links prove against `prev_center` and the current passes. The entries read the posted moves (`plunge_law::column_cleared`). So the mix between levels keeps its proofs. `cleared_links` stays on for a fallback level, so `through_cut` also applies to the Auto passes there. That is stricter, so it can only lift more. The pre-drilled re-seat stays off, which is also the safer side. The fallback note goes through the same `b.note` / `notes` channel as the other "Pass start" notes (`pocket.rs`, `pocket_avoid.rs`).

Note (minor): in `pocket_avoid`, two levels with different areas give two different fallback texts. The `!notes.contains(n)` filter then keeps both.

## 3. Inside with no hole

`core_first` (lines 191-208) gives the part's rings core first, marked `core`. `order` does not judge them for full width and adds `core_note`. If no part has a start side, `started` stays false and `level_pieces` returns `None`, so the old Auto plan runs (line 152). This agrees with the earlier rule.

## 4. Checks kept

The delta in `level_order.rs` adds only the `core` field, the count and the note. `linkable` with `chord_clears(center, e, s)`, `lead_in`, `through_cut`, `pass_link` and the entry and refusal law did not change. My points 1, 3 and 4 of comment 7079896741 stay valid.

## 5. Auto

`git diff origin/main a91eb11d3 -- crates/motion/src/machining2d/waterscan.rs` is empty. No golden file is in the diff. `level_pieces` returns `None` for Auto before any part is read. `non_sliver_center` moved to `pocket_plan.rs` with no change to its body, and its test moved with it.

## 6. Tests

- `the_stock_inside_a_ring_part_is_cut_whole` and `a_pocket_with_a_hollow_boss_is_cut_whole`, for Outside and Inside: `assert_no_overcut` against the reach, and `assert_bounded_leftover(area(unreachable) + 8.0, Some(unreachable))`. `unreachable` is the material less its opening by the tool disc, grown by 0.2 mm. So no interior cell may stay uncut outside the corners that the tool cannot reach, and the total stays at most that corner area plus 8 mm² of edge raster.
- The "Do not touch" pin: `assert_bounded_leftover(60.0, Some(pin + 1.5))`. Uncut cells are permitted only in the keep-out band.
- Guard unit test `the_guard_reads_a_standing_core_and_passes_a_whole_plan`: a lone ring leaves about 113 mm² (core radius 6), a complete plan leaves at most `LEFT_TOL`, and NaN is refused.
- `clip_line` has a new test for a vertex on the boundary, a tangent touch and an overlap along an edge in mid-segment. That closes the test gap from my first read.
- No test makes the guard fall back from a real plan, and no test reads the fallback note on a path.

Law: no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test code in the delta. File lengths: `level_rings.rs` 324, `level_order.rs` 300, `pocket.rs` 343, `pocket_plan.rs` 95, `clip_line.rs` 306. The PR is still a draft, and its body has `Process change: yes`.

## Not judged without a run

- The readings (2.57 / 2.63 / 15.1 / 15.2 / 10.8 mm²) and the claim of 0 interior cells.
- How often the guard falls back on real parts, and the cost of `Region::sweep` on large areas.
- A fallback level inside `pocket_avoid` (no fixture makes one).
- The heavy plan (243 steps, 0 failed, as the author reports).

New head: 3c3f13eb4.

Finding fixed: the completeness guard's fallback note did not carry `RINGS_FALLBACK`. `rings_fallbacks()` counted zero, so the 2D Offset posted no `StrategyFallback` warning when it fell back to the Auto order. The note now carries `RINGS_FALLBACK`. The op posts one advisory `StrategyFallback` warning plus the "Pass start" note. This is the WARN law that the maintainer set for the pass-start family.

The branch also has a clean merge of `origin/main`. The merge adds the #3035 warning law (`RINGS_FALLBACK`, `rings_fallbacks`, `Warning::StrategyFallback`).

Pins:
- `machining2d::pass_start::tests::the_guard_fallback_is_an_offset_rings_fallback`
- `app offset_pass_start::the_offset_guard_fallback_is_a_strategy_fallback`
- `app offset_pass_start::fig8_inside_offset_names_its_part_wall_start` now asserts that a complete band posts no fallback warning.

Gate (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`, `--base origin/main`):
- `motion suites: lib`: ok, 221 s.
- `app suites: offset_pass_start`: ok, 61 s, 4 passed and 2 ignored (heavy lane).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The quick tier falls back to the full batch plan because the branch touches `camcraft-geometry`. I ran the two touched steps with `--only`; both are green. The shared geometry was gated on a91eb11d3, and the merge of main is conflict-free.

Not exercised: no fixture makes the offset guard fall back on a real area. The posting law for a fallback note is pinned by `strategy_fallback`; the offset note and its count are pinned directly. The warning text still reads "Adaptive fell back to Offset rings", while the "Pass start" note carries the accurate text. A neutral text for the 2D family is a possible follow-up.

Coordinator: the head moved to 3c3f13eb4 after the gate started (the trial merge and the 243-step heavy run were on a91eb11d3). The gate repeats on the new head. Please push no more to this branch until it merges, or say so here first.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 3c3f13eb4f8a1d24717b3dce9fb4addd6c38eec9 -->
